title: Const generic parameters M, N, T not validated for overflow safety
description:
## Locations
- /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/wire.rs line 22-33
- /Volumes/Attic/Desktop/Projects/crates/schc/src/fragment/ack_on_error.rs line 32-38

## Problem
Functions like `fcn_max<N>()`, `window_max<M>()`, and `bitmap_size<N>()` compute values using bit shifts:

```rust
pub const fn fcn_max<const N: u8>() -> u8 {
    (1u8 << N) - 1
}
pub const fn bitmap_size<const N: u8>() -> usize {
    1usize << N
}
```

If N >= 8, the u8 shift overflows (wraps or panics depending on build mode).
If N >= 64, the usize shift can overflow on 64-bit platforms.
If M or N is 0, some calculations produce unexpected results (e.g., fcn_max::<0>() = 0).

## API Risk
Users specifying const generics at call sites (e.g., `Fragment::<2, 128, 1>`) will get compile-time or runtime errors that are hard to diagnose. The library does not guard against invalid parameter combinations.

## Suggested Fix
Add static assertions or const-evaluable checks:
```rust
const _: () = assert!(N <= 7, "N must be <= 7 for u8 FCN values");
const _: () = assert!(M <= 2, "M must be <= 2 for practical window counts");
```
